text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Employee organisations and workers are gearing up for a mass protest of the Islamist-led government.
- The richest people in Turkey earn eleven times as much as the poorest.
MILLIYET
- Islamist-led government, fed up by opposition pressure, ask the far-right Grand Unity Party to join them ahead of early elections.
- A "poverty summit", organised the United Nations and a Turkish business group, will to begin on Thursday in the underdeveloped southeastern town of Diyarbakir.
HURRIYET
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan says he will not give the premiership to his coalition partner Tansu Ciller earlier than the agreed date in 1998.
- Azeri caviar will be introduced on the international market by Turkish businessmen.
YENI YUZYIL
- Ciller cheerfully announced "wheat prices" following a crucial meeting with Erbakan, to the disappointment of all those expecting them to come up with a solution to the extended political turmoil.
- The Eurogold gold company has not given up work on a mine in Bergama despite a decision by the court of appeals to shut their gold mine because of the use of cyanide.
RADIKAL
- A Turkish court ordered the arrest of five policemen for being involved in the killing of Metin Goktepe, a leftist journalist allegedly beaten to death in police custody.
- Erbakan does not agree to a plan for a tax-free minimum wage as he vowed earlier because he cannot sacrifice the 400 trillion ($2,9 milion) Turkish lira raised by the tax on the minimum wage.
DUNYA
- The state-owned Maritime Authority is to be sold off under the government's privatisation scheme.
ZAMAN
- The supreme election board says Turkey can be ready for early general election in a four months' time at the cost of two trillion lira ($14,300).
CUMHURIYET
- The implementation of a military-sponspored education plan to increase compulsory education to eight years from the current five can be considered after possible early elections. $1=140,200
